title: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing in Jacksonville, FL
metaDescription: Medical office replacement sourcing for Jacksonville 1031 exchanges, run as a scoped submittal package that qualifies each MOB before the 45-day deadline.

sections.html: A Jacksonville exchange into a medical office building starts the same way a bid package starts: with a scope of work, not a property tour. Before any candidate building gets shown to an investor, the sourcing scope defines tenant mix, lease structure, and location tier, so the properties that reach the desk have already cleared a first round of qualification rather than being screened live against the clock.

sections.heading: Scoping the Package Before the 45-Day Clock Starts
sections.html:
The scope of work for a medical office search is written before the relinquished property closes, not after. It sets the acceptable building class, the minimum remaining lease term on anchor tenants, and whether single-tenant or multi-tenant medical office fits the investor's hold strategy, so the 45-day identification window is spent confirming candidates against a fixed spec rather than debating what the spec should be.

That scope also fixes a submarket radius up front. A Southside search and a Northside search pull from different tenant rosters and different lease terms, and mixing the two mid-search slows the package down instead of widening it usefully.

sections.heading: Where Jacksonville's Medical Office Stock Concentrates
sections.html:
Jacksonville's medical office inventory clusters around its hospital systems: the Baptist Health and UF Health corridors near the Southbank and San Marco, the Mayo Clinic campus on the Southside, and smaller single-tenant clinics serving the population around Naval Station Mayport and NAS Jacksonville. Each cluster carries a different tenant profile, from large health-system-affiliated leases to independent practice groups renewing on shorter terms.

A sourcing package built for Jacksonville has to account for that split, since a health-system-anchored building underwrites differently than a standalone practice building even when the asking cap rates look similar on paper.

sections.heading: The Submittal Package Each Candidate Has to Clear
sections.html:
Every candidate building moves through the same checklist before it is added to the written identification, so the file stays consistent regardless of which broker sourced the lead.

  • Current rent roll with tenant specialty and lease expiration dates
  • Certificate of occupancy and medical-use zoning confirmation
  • Lease abstracts for any tenant occupying more than 20 percent of rentable area
  • Recent capital expenditure history, particularly HVAC and parking lot condition
  • Title commitment and survey ordered ahead of the identification deadline

sections.heading: Reading Lease Term Against the Exchange Timeline
sections.html:
A medical office building with a tenant rolling within eighteen months carries different debt-service coverage than one with a ten-year health-system lease, and that difference has to be priced into the replacement decision, not discovered after closing. Duval County's consolidated assessment approach also means the tax basis on a newly acquired MOB can shift meaningfully at the next reassessment cycle, which is worth confirming with the investor's advisor before the offer is submitted.

Because Florida carries no state income tax, out-of-state investors exchanging into a Jacksonville medical office are weighing that against their home-state treatment separately, and that comparison sits with the investor's own tax advisor rather than the sourcing team.

sections.heading: Closing Out the File Once a Candidate Is Selected
sections.html: Once a building is selected from the identified list, the submittal package converts into a closing file: lease estoppels requested from each tenant, the qualified intermediary notified of the specific parcel, and the purchase contract reviewed for assignment language before signature. Closing the file the same way on every deal, rather than reconstructing the checklist each time, is what keeps a medical office acquisition on schedule inside the 180-day exchange period.

faqs.q: What makes medical office buildings different to source than general office space?
faqs.a: Medical office tenants require plumbing, parking ratios, and sometimes radiology shielding that general office space does not, so a building's physical fit for medical use has to be confirmed before it goes on the identification list. A space that reads as office on paper can fail a medical-use walk-through for reasons that never show up in a rent roll.

faqs.q: How does a health-system-anchored lease change underwriting versus an independent practice tenant?
faqs.a: A lease backed by a hospital system generally carries stronger credit and longer average terms, while independent practice leases renew more frequently and depend more on the individual physician group's stability. Both can work inside a 1031 exchange, but the debt-service assumptions and renewal risk differ enough that they should be modeled separately.

faqs.q: Can a medical office building purchased mid-exchange still be re-tenanted later?
faqs.a: Yes, re-tenanting after the exchange closes is a normal operating decision and does not affect the completed exchange. What matters for exchange qualification is that the replacement property was correctly identified and acquired within the 45-day and 180-day windows, not what the investor does with tenancy afterward.

faqs.q: Does Jacksonville's hospital footprint concentrate medical office demand in specific corridors?
faqs.a: Demand concentrates near the Southbank, San Marco, and Southside corridors closest to the major hospital campuses, with a secondary cluster of smaller practice buildings spread near Naval Station Mayport and NAS Jacksonville serving military and civilian medical staffing. A sourcing search benefits from naming a corridor rather than searching the county broadly.

faqs.q: What capital expenditure items get flagged most often in medical office due diligence?
faqs.a: HVAC systems sized for medical-grade air exchange rates and parking lot condition come up most often, since both are expensive to defer and directly affect tenant retention. Reviewing recent capital expenditure history before submitting an offer avoids a surprise special assessment shortly after closing.

faqs.q: How does the submittal package change for a multi-tenant medical building versus a single-tenant clinic?
faqs.a: A multi-tenant building requires reviewing lease abstracts and estoppels for every practice group on the rent roll, while a single-tenant clinic concentrates that same review into one lease and one tenant's financial standing. The underlying checklist stays the same, but a multi-tenant file simply takes longer to assemble before it can be added to the identification list.
